countries.summary: Richtwertmietzins (reference value rent) for Altbau in the MRG full-application area, set per Bundesland and valorised annually on 1 April (published by Statistik Austria since 2026). Since 1 Jan 2026 the Mieten-Wertsicherungsgesetz (MieWeG, BGBl I 114/2025) additionally caps contractual indexation in every residential lease inside MRG scope: full CPI up to 3%, only half of the excess above 3%. Statutory ceilings on the regulated valorisation: 0% in 2024 and 2025, 1% on 1.4.2026, 2% on 1.4.2027, then the 3%+half rule from 1.4.2028.

lateFee.notes: Default interest 4% p.a. (§ 1000 ABGB); a higher agreed rate is reducible (§ 1336(2) ABGB, § 6(1)(13) KSchG). A flat fee is void unless itemised per collection step and fault-based (OGH RS0129621). The 8-day demand period is § 30(2)(1) MRG. Advisory — verify locally.

rules.notes: 5. MILG / MieWeG, BGBl I Nr. 114/2025 (in force 1 Jan 2026): RichtWG § 5 Abs 2 and MRG § 16 Abs 6 cap the 1-Apr-2027 valorisation of Richtwerte and Kategoriebetraege at 2% over the last change date; MieWeG § 1 Abs 3 mirrors it for contractual Wertsicherung in price-regulated leases. Ceiling, not a fixed step — actual = min(VPI 2010 annual average change 2026, 2%), published by Statistik Austria on 1 Apr 2027. From 1 Apr 2028 the permanent rule applies: inflation above 3% counts only half for the excess.

MRG-Vollausnahme (§ 1 Abs 2 MRG): flats in Ein- und Zweiobjekthaeusern (Z 5), Freizeit-/Zweitwohnungen (Z 4), Dienst- and Beherbergungswohnungen. Fully free rent and free contractual indexation — these leases are OUTSIDE the MRG and therefore outside the MieWeG cap that applies from 1 Jan 2026. Note: freifinanzierte Neubauten with Baubewilligung after 30.6.1953 are NOT in this group — they are MRG § 1 Abs 4 Teilanwendung and their indexation IS capped by MieWeG (see the separate free-sector rule). WGG leases are excluded from MieWeG by its § 1 Abs 6 unless the rent follows § 13 Abs 4 WGG.

MieWeG § 1 Abs 2 (5. MILG, BGBl I 114/2025, in force 1 Jan 2026): contractual Wertsicherung in residential leases in the MRG full and partial application area — including freifinanzierte Neubauten under § 1 Abs 4 MRG — may be exercised only once a year with effect from 1 April, by the VPI 2020 annual average change of the preceding calendar year, with the part above 3 percentage points counted only half. VPI 2025 annual average = 3.6% (Statistik Austria), so the maximum on 1 Apr 2026 is 3.30%. Applies to pre-2026 contracts too (§ 4 Abs 2); a clause more unfavourable to the tenant is capped down, not void (§ 1 Abs 4). First indexation after contract conclusion is pro-rated by full months (§ 1 Abs 2 Z 2). Does not apply to MRG-Vollausnahmen or to WGG leases (§ 1 Abs 6). Price-regulated leases are additionally capped at 1% (2026) / 2% (2027) by § 1 Abs 3. Type CAP_OVER_INDEX chosen as closest existing constant for an indexed rise with a statutory half-counting cap.

5. MILG / MieWeG (BGBl I 114/2025): the 1-Apr-2026 valorisation of Richtwerte and Kategoriebetraege is capped at 1% (RichtWG § 5 Abs 2); uncapped VPI 2025 annual average was 3.6%, so the cap bound. First valorisation since 2023 (2024 and 2025 were suspended). Richtwerte from 1 Apr 2026 (EUR/m2): Bgld 6.15, Ktn 7.89, NOe 6.92, OOe 7.30, Sbg 9.31, Stmk 9.30, Tirol 8.22, Vbg 10.35, Wien 6.74; Kategoriebetraege A 4.51 / B 3.38 / C 2.25 / D brauchbar 2.25 / D unbrauchbar 1.13. Statistik Austria now publishes these (previously BMJ Kundmachung). The 2027 ceiling of 2% is already enacted. Increases take effect at the earliest with the next Zinstermin after a written Erhoehungsbegehren.

4. MILG (BGBl I 12/2025): the 1-Apr-2025 valorisation of Richtwerte and Kategoriebetraege was suspended entirely — '1. April 2025 und' was struck from RichtWG § 5 Abs 2. The +4.2% (Richtwert) / +2.9% (Kategorie) otherwise due did not take effect. The 5% ceiling planned by the 3. MILG was superseded before it applied. Next valorisation: 1 Apr 2026.
3. MILG: Richtwert- und Kategorievalorisierung für 2024 ausgesetzt (no statutory adjustment).

Regional overlays: Brussels caps initial rent at reference rent +20% (art. 224/1 Housing Code, in force 1 May 2025) and applies an EPC E/F/G correction factor to pre-14-Oct-2022 leases; Flanders applies a permanent EPC D/E/F correction factor to pre-1-Oct-2022 leases; Wallonia has had no EPC restriction since 1 Nov 2023.

lateFee.notes: Brussels prohibits late-payment indemnity clauses outright for leases concluded or renewed from 1 Nov 2024 (art. 225/1 Code du Logement). In Flanders and Wallonia a landlord acting as an undertaking is capped by the Book XIX WER scale (EUR 20; EUR 30 + 10%; EUR 65 + 5%, max EUR 2,000) after a free 14-day reminder; otherwise the court reduces an unreasonable clause (art. 5.88 BW). Legal interest 4.5% (2026). Advisory — verify locally.

lateFee.notes: England: the Tenant Fees Act 2019 makes a flat late fee a prohibited payment; only interest at 3% above the Bank of England base rate may be charged, once rent is 14 or more days late and only if the tenancy agreement provides for it. Wales applies the same rate from 7 days. Scotland and Northern Ireland have no equivalent regime. Advisory — verify locally.

rules.additionalConditions: From 1 May 2026 rent may be increased only by a section 13 notice on the prescribed Form 4A, at most once in any 12-month period, with at least 2 months' notice, and not at all during the first year of the tenancy. The new rent may not exceed open market rent. Contractual rent-review clauses and informal rent reviews have no effect. The tenant may apply free of charge to the First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber); the tribunal cannot set a rent above the figure the landlord proposed, cannot backdate the increase (the new rent applies from the date of determination) and may defer the increase by up to a further 2 months where payment would cause undue hardship. Periodic assured tenancies replace fixed-term ASTs and section 21 is abolished. A landlord may require at most 1 month's rent in advance (28 days where the rental period is under a month) once the tenancy agreement is signed. Code-registered purpose-built student accommodation is outside the assured tenancy regime; private student HMOs are in scope.
rules.notes: Renters' Rights Act 2025 (2025 c. 26) received Royal Assent on 27 October 2025; the tenancy-reform provisions, including the new section 13 rent procedure, apply to new and existing tenancies from 1 May 2026. Before 1 May 2026 the old section 13 procedure (1 month's notice, tribunal able to set a higher rent, contractual rent reviews valid) still applied. Market-based rent is retained — there is no statutory percentage cap in England.

rules.additionalConditions: Max one rent increase per 12 months; 3 months written notice. Department reserve power to extend 12-month protection up to 2 years (not yet exercised).
rules.notes: No statutory percentage cap. Renters' Rights Act 2025 does not extend to NI (housing is devolved).

rules.additionalConditions: No statutory percentage cap in 2026. Private residential tenancy rules apply: rent may be increased only once in any 12-month period, on at least 3 months' written notice using the prescribed rent-increase notice. The tenant may refer the increase to Rent Service Scotland within 21 days; the rent officer determines open market rent and the figure set may be higher or lower than the amount the landlord proposed. The rent control area framework (CPI + 1%, capped at 6% per year, applying both within and between tenancies, one increase per 12 months) is not yet operative: from 1 April 2026 local authorities must assess rent conditions in their area, with first reports due to Scottish Ministers no later than 31 May 2027 and designations expected from 2027. A designation lasts a maximum of 5 years. Regulations exempt mid-market rent and build-to-rent properties.
rules.notes: Housing (Scotland) Act 2025 (2025 asp 13) received Royal Assent 6 November 2025; rent control area powers commenced 1 April 2026 but no rent control area is designated during 2026. Previous sourceUrl (legislation.gov.uk/asp/2025/housing-scotland-act) returned HTTP 404; correct citation is legislation.gov.uk/asp/2025/13/contents. Exemptions per the Private Housing Rent Control (Exempt Property) (Scotland) Regulations 2026 are mid-market rent and build-to-rent; purpose-built student accommodation is outside the PRT regime rather than an exemption.

rules.additionalConditions: Rent under a periodic standard occupation contract may be varied no more than once in any 12-month period, on at least 2 months' written notice. This is a fundamental term of the contract and cannot be contracted out of. No statutory cap.
rules.notes: Market-based; no rent control in force or planned for 2026. The October 2024 White Paper on Adequate Housing, Fair Rents and Affordability declined to introduce rent controls and deferred any housing-adequacy legislation to the next Senedd term.
Renters Rights Bill expected to pass. Section 21 abolition planned.

rules.additionalConditions: From 1 April 2025 a landlord cannot increase rent within 12 months of granting the tenancy, nor within 12 months of the last rent increase, and must give at least 3 months' written notice. Written notice may be given electronically (email, text or other electronic communication). A second increase inside a 12-month period has no legal effect and the tenant is not obliged to pay it.
rules.notes: Section 7 (Regulation of Rent) of the Private Tenancies Act (NI) 2022 came into operation on 1 April 2025, not 1 April 2023. No statutory percentage cap; the power to make regulations to freeze or cut rents lapsed under the Act's sunset clause on 28 October 2023. The Renters' Rights Act 2025 does not extend to Northern Ireland (housing is devolved).

rules.additionalConditions: No statutory percentage cap from 1 April 2025. Rent may be increased only once in any 12-month period, on at least 3 months' written notice. On referral to Rent Service Scotland the rent is set at open market rent and may be higher or lower than the rent the landlord proposed.
rules.notes: The temporary tapered rent-adjudication formula (6% plus 0.33% per percentage point of market gap above 6%, capped at 12%) expired on 31 March 2025 and was not renewed, so no percentage cap applies from 1 April 2025. Transitory protections continued only for referrals made before 1 April 2025. The 12% formula remains recorded on the 2024 row, which covers 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025.

Market rent. Renters Reform Bill progressing.

Rent review notice must be served at least 90 days before the new rent takes effect; since 14 Sep 2026 a copy must reach the RTB within 7 days of service on the tenant (previously same day) or the notice is invalid. CPI annual rate was 3.7% in the 12 months to August 2026 (CSO, released 10 Sep 2026), so the binding cap is currently 2%.

rules.additionalConditions: Reset to open market rent is permitted ONLY where the previous rent was below market value AND one statutory ground applies: the last tenant ended the tenancy by choice; the tenant breached their obligations; the home no longer met the tenant's needs; it is the first tenancy in the property; no tenancy existed for at least 2 years (1 year for a protected structure); the property was substantially renovated and re-offered to the previous tenant; the 6-year tenancy cycle ended. A reset is BLOCKED where the previous tenancy ended by a no-fault termination (landlord selling, occupying personally, or changing the property's use). If no ground applies, the existing capped rent carries over and only the 2%/CPI cap may be applied.
rules.notes: Applies to tenancies created on or after 2026-03-01. The new rent must be market rent evidenced from the RTB Rent Register: the rent setting notice must cite three similar properties. The rent setting notice is served at the start of the tenancy and must be submitted to the RTB within one month of the tenancy start date - the 90-day advance notice and the 7-day RTB copy rule apply to rent REVIEW notices, not to rent setting on a new tenancy. After the reset, subsequent annual increases fall back under the 2%/CPI cap.

rules.additionalConditions: Rent ceiling: annual rent may not exceed 5% of the capital invested in the dwelling (Art. 3(1), loi modifiée du 21 septembre 2006). Invested capital is revalued at lease signature or at rent adaptation with the revaluation coefficients of art. 102, al. 6 of the loi modifiée du 4 décembre 1967 (LIR) - not a STATEC construction-cost index. If the dwelling is 15 years old or more, the revalued capital (land price excluded) is reduced by 2% per additional two-year period, unless the landlord proves equivalent maintenance/repair spending. Furnished lettings may add a furniture supplement of at most 1.5% of the furniture invoices (invoices under 10 years old only). Rent may be adapted only every two years (Art. 3(5) al. 1) and no single adaptation may exceed 10% (Art. 3(5) al. 3); if the landlord asks for more, the excess is not owed from the term following the tenant's registered-letter objection. Automatic CPI indexation clauses are not permitted, but remain effective until the tenant objects by registered letter.
